$comment: c112 (D-FFI-PE-IMPORT-THUNK): the address-taken-import RUN witness. A static-init array holds the ADDRESS of an imported function (`puts`) -- sqlite's os_win.c aSyscall[] shape -- and main CALLS it indirectly (a `volatile` load so neither the baseline nor the release arm can fold the indirect call into a direct `puts(...)`, keeping the address-taken path live at runtime). Every hosted format must produce a CALLABLE address for an address-taken import. ELF and Mach-O executables give the import's canonical address; on PE the slot is, since P69 (design c2, D-LK-LIBRARY-FUNCTION-ADDRESS-IS-THE-IMAGE-STUB), the FirstThunk of an import descriptor of its own, so the LOADER writes `puts`'s own address into it -- the value GetProcAddress answers, compared by examples/c/library_function_address_equals_getprocaddress. (From c112 until then the slot held the image's synthesized `jmp *[IAT slot]` import THUNK: callable, but not the function's address; before c112 it held the raw IAT data slot and the call executed data as code.) A correct run prints the line and exits 42. RED-on-disable: stop emitting the slot's own import descriptor in pe.cpp -> the slot keeps its lookup entry, an RVA -> the indirect call faults (no exit 42). The elf/arm64 legs already ran this construct green (sqlite on Linux, c91/c93), so all three legs prove the same source runs everywhere.
